items.title: Over a ring whose localizations satisfy the Warfield conditions every finitely presented module is a summand of a finite sum of quotients by principal ideals
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma assumes that every local ring of R at a maximal ideal satisfies the equivalent conditions of the generalized-valuation-ring lemma, and concludes that every finitely presented R-module is a summand of a finite direct sum of modules of the form R/fR (source lines 37736-37746). The proof is a genuine local-to-global argument. It reduces the conclusion to showing that Hom_R(M, B) -> Hom_R(M, C) is surjective for every short exact sequence with the property fA = A cap fB for all f, which is the characterisation established by the preceding module lemma (proof lines 37749-37757). Surjectivity is then checked after localization at maximal ideals, using that the localized sequences inherit the condition because an element of a localization can be written as a unit times an element of R and localization is exact, and using that the Hom modules localize for finitely presented M (proof lines 37758-37772). The conclusion at each maximal ideal is exactly the hypothesis, reduced through the localized modules lemma (proof lines 37773-37778). The final step is what makes the direct sum finite: since M is a finite R-module its image in the potentially infinite direct sum lies in a finite sub-sum (proof lines 37780-37785). The two non-routine moves are the localization of the condition fA = A cap fB and the finiteness bookkeeping at the end.
